title: Classes & Objects
description: Blueprints, objects, instance vs static, and who can touch what.

questions.explanation: n is static — one shared copy. The constructor ran twice, so n is 2.

options: name is private — outside code can't touch it directly
questions.explanation: private blocks direct access from outside the class. You'd need a setter like setName().

questions.prompt: Order these from first to last when an object is created.
lines: Reference is assigned to the variable
questions.explanation: Memory first, fields get defaults, the constructor runs, then the reference is assigned.

questions.prompt: Creating an object needs the ___ keyword.
questions.explanation: new allocates the memory and runs the constructor.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.definition: Blueprint that objects are built from
One instance built from a class
Special method that runs at creation
Belongs to the class, shared by all objects

questions.explanation: Class = blueprint, object = instance, constructor = setup, static = shared.

questions.prompt: Which JavaScript is the same class?
questions.explanation: Java's constructor becomes JavaScript's constructor() method — same idea, different keyword.
The constructor overwrote the field initializer — name is now "Miso".

options: A constructor can't have a return type — this is just a method
questions.explanation: The moment you add 'int', it's an ordinary method that happens to share the class name.
static = one copy shared by every object of the class.

questions.prompt: Which Java version matches this JavaScript?
questions.explanation: Fields declared with types, a same-name constructor, and a typed method — the Java mirror of the JS class.
